comment: The Mermaid grammar of this repository, written from its specification (packages/spec/docs). This file holds the rules that every diagram type shares; grammar/diagrams/<type>.grammar.json holds the rules of one diagram type, one file per document of packages/spec/docs/diagrams/; src/grammar.ts puts them together into one grammar. The `comment` of each rule explains what the rule reads, then names the sections of the specification that it follows, as `Follows <document>.md#<section>.`; where a rule approximates a section beyond the limits below, the comment says what it leaves out. `{{name}}` in a regular expression stands for the value of `variables`, the convention of the variables of Sublime Text's sublime-syntax files; src/grammar.ts resolves references between variables before substituting them. Case-insensitive comparisons follow the notation in common.md#notation; src/grammar.ts puts Oniguruma's whole-pattern ASCII-only ignore-case option at the head of every regular expression; Shiki's JavaScript engine does not support this option. A common variable stands for a form that common.md or detection.md defines, for a part of a shared rule that a diagram rule must also see, or for a part that a shared rule and its variant share. A form that a diagram's own document defines stays in that diagram. Common variable ownership: `ws`: common.md#notation defines Notation whitespace. `lws`: common.md#notation defines line whitespace as whitespace outside a line terminator. `separators`: common.md#notation excludes the line separator and paragraph separator from line terminators and includes them among the boundaries of a line segment. `wordEnd`: common.md#notation defines a word as a maximal run of ASCII letters, ASCII digits or underscore; common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary reads text without directives, so the lookahead prevents a word character after any following directives from continuing it. `directiveStart`: common.md#where-a-directive-is says a directive starts at a percent pair and opening brace when optional whitespace and a word character follow. `directiveName`: common.md#where-a-directive-is defines the name as a word. `directiveWordArgument`: common.md#where-a-directive-is takes a word argument when its first character is a word character. `directiveFreeTextArgument`: common.md#where-a-directive-is takes other argument text through before the first closer, line separator, paragraph separator or end of text, leaving whitespace before the closer outside the argument. `directiveEnd`: common.md#where-a-directive-is defines the optional closing brace and percent pair. `directive`: common.md#where-a-directive-is defines the complete directive, including its whitespace, optional colon, argument and optional closer. These expressions approximate multiline directives one physical line at a time. `directives`: common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary says every subsequent rule reads the text without its directives. `gap`: common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary says directives in whitespace do not lie inside a unit, with the whitespace set of common.md#notation. `asciiGap`: the same sentence permits directives among ASCII spaces and tabs. `lineGap`: the same sentence permits directives among the line whitespace of common.md#notation. `requiredGap`: that sentence preserves a required Notation whitespace character rather than letting a directive supply it. `requiredAsciiGap`: the same sentence preserves a required ASCII space or tab. `requiredLineGap`: the same sentence preserves a required line whitespace character. `whitespaceStart`: common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary allows directives before a required whitespace character without supplying that character; common.md#notation defines its whitespace set. `whitespaceSeparator`: the same sentence allows directives before and after exactly one Notation whitespace character. `spaceSeparator`: the same sentence allows directives before and after exactly one ASCII space. `lineText`: common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary reads text without its directives; common.md#notation defines a line segment as excluding physical line terminators, line separator and paragraph separator. `physicalLineText`: the same directive sentence applies to a line, which common.md#notation defines as excluding physical line terminators only. The type rules retain their own choices of these text and whitespace forms. `entity`: common.md#entities defines a number sign, a word and a semicolon, in text without directives. `stringEscape`: packet.md#numbers-and-strings and architecture.md#icons-strings-and-bracketed-labels define a backslash and one character other than LF, CR, LS or PS; common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary reads through whole directives. This part of string-escaped is also needed by its HTML variant and architecture's complete quoted-label lookahead. `markdownStringEnd`: usecase.md#ordered-default-context-rules ends markdown at a backquote followed by a double quote, through directives; the shared markdown string, Flowchart and Agentflow markdown strings, and HTML variants use the same closer. `htmlTagStart`: common.md#html-attribute-quotes defines an opening angle bracket and a tag name, provided a closing angle bracket follows; the expression looks on the same line. `htmlQuotedValueStart`: common.md#html-attribute-quotes defines equals followed by a double quote whose matching double quote precedes the tag closer; the expression looks on the same line. `htmlTagEnd`: common.md#html-attribute-quotes says the attribute part ends at the first >; common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary says a directive is trivia and not diagram text. Read a > or a whole directive containing > as the tag end. Only a free-text directive argument can contain >; the lookahead reads the directive prefix atomically and looks for > before its closer or a separator, then the shared directive expression reads it whole. This part is also needed by the flowchart and agentflow HTML helpers. `htmlTagDirective`: the same sentences read a directive without > whole inside the tag. `htmlTagCharacter`: those sentences and common.md#comment-lines read one character outside a directive, a separator-led common comment, a double quote, > or a physical line terminator. `htmlTagCharacterPreservedComments`: common.md#mermaidjs-and-this-specification says agentflow and eventmodeling receive comment lines, so this variant retains comment-looking text. `htmlQuotedValue` and `htmlQuotedValuePreservedComments`: common.md#html-attribute-quotes reads from equals and a double quote through its matching double quote; read directives whole, stopping before the tag end or the applicable common-comment boundary. The shared HTML rules use these parts, including their markdown variants, which stop only before the markdown closer outside quoted values and directives. `htmlTagBackslashBeforeQuotedValue`: common.md#html-attribute-quotes finds quoted values in the text as written, so a preceding backslash cannot consume the equals sign of their opener. `htmlTagStringEscape`: packet.md#numbers-and-strings and common.md#html-attribute-quotes read a backslash, zero or more directives without a tag end (htmlTagDirective), and one character other than a closing angle bracket, LF, CR, line separator or paragraph separator. The final character cannot start a directive, so a directive containing the tag end is left whole for the enclosing string. This escape cannot hold a common-comment start: its character is no separator, and a directive's free text stops before one. `commentDirectiveWhitespace`: common.md#comment-lines ends the native comment body before a separator-led common comment, including in a directive's whitespace. `commentDirective` assembles the shared directive parts with that bounded whitespace; its name, word argument and free-text argument already cannot contain that boundary. `commentBodyPart`: the body part shared by native-percent-comment and hidden-directive reads commentDirective or one physical-line character that starts neither a directive nor a separator-led common comment. `hiddenDirectiveStart` and `hiddenDirectiveEnd`: the opener and qualifying closer shared by hidden-directive and its comment-preserving variant; eventmodeling.md#native-hidden-forms-and-comments reads %%{ through the first }%% followed by Notation whitespace or end of text. `hiddenYamlBegin` and `hiddenYamlEnd`: the fences and boundary shared by hidden-yaml and its comment-preserving variant; eventmodeling.md#native-hidden-forms-and-comments opens with three dashes, optional ASCII space/tab and LF, and closes at an unindented three-dash fence followed by Notation whitespace or end of text; common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary leaves a directive before its first dash outside the indentation. common.md#mermaidjs-and-this-specification says agentflow and eventmodeling receive comment lines, so the preserving variants retain comment-looking text. `htmlTag`, `htmlTagEscaped` and `htmlTagPreservedComments`: common.md#html-attribute-quotes defines a tag name and attribute part and converts the double quotes of quoted attribute values; these expressions assemble the same-line parts for the shared rules and diagram lookaheads. The escaped variant also reads htmlTagStringEscape outside quoted values; its ordinary-character alternative excludes stringEscape so a backslash cannot be reread as an ordinary character. `nonDirectivePercentPair`: common.md#comment-lines distinguishes percent pairs belonging to a comment from directives. `commonLineValueEnd`: common.md#comment-lines makes a line separator or paragraph separator followed only by whitespace and directives before a comment end the surrounding value before that separator; the shared composite line forms also stop at their first non-directive percent pair or physical line end, as stated in packet.md#composite-common-forms and the matching common-form sentences cited by common-statements. `lineValueEnd`: common.md#comment-lines ends a line value before a separator-led common comment or at physical line end. `separatorCommentEnd`: common.md#comment-lines supplies only the separator-led common-comment boundary, without a type-specific value ending. `commonStatementStart`: the explicitly shared common forms, packet.md#composite-common-forms and the matching common-form sentences cited by common-statements, begin at unit positions with optional ASCII spaces or tabs. The expression recognizes line start, the current scanning position, and positions after a closing brace or any directive closer, within the unit-start limitation below. `diagramStart`: common.md#leading-whitespace makes whitespace, directives and comment regions before the first unit trivia; common.md#diagram-detection and detection.md#how-to-read-the-list place header detection at the position reached after those removals. The expression recognizes line start or a position after a directive closer and reads remaining Notation whitespace. Each diagram block begins at its header and runs to the end of the text (its `end` never matches): the diagram type is chosen once, from the header (detection.md), and the rest of the text is its body. The limits that hold for every rule: the grammar reads line by line: a form whose components, gaps or value cross a line break (whitespace including line feeds, a value starting on the next line, or a string, label or comment block read by a single match rule) is read only on its own line. It does not check acceptance: rejected input (an unclosed form, a required but empty value, a character a unit does not admit, or a wrong count) may be colored as accepted, and a begin/end scope without its closer stays open to the end of the text. The quotes that common.md#html-attribute-quotes changes are read as changed only by html-tag inside a double-quoted string or a label that holds the whole tag. Where a tag starts in an earlier unit of the line (C4 Person(<b,"x="Person">")), and where a changed quote would end or start a single-quoted string (treemap '<b x="title">'), the quotes are read as written: a rule cannot see a tag that began in an earlier unit, and the end of an open scope cannot depend on what a rule inside it read. Unit starts are not tracked after an ordinary match: a following statement or unit on the same line is recognized only at positions a rule names (line start, right after the header, right after a directive, or right after a closing delimiter); text units left without a scope are not tokenized. Native hidden YAML and hidden directive forms inside some bodies are colored as comments. The frontmatter rule cannot know whether a line is the first line or has a line terminator. The `;` that the `style` and `classDef` line rule ignores (common.md#style-and-classdef-lines) is colored as the rules around it read it: whether a `;` is ignored depends on the text before it on its line segment and on the rest of the segment, so every rule that stops at a `;` would have to know it, while a TextMate rule sees the text before its match only through a lookbehind of fixed length. A line separator or paragraph separator that the whitespace after a directive's argument takes (common.md#where-a-directive-is) is still read as a comment start: whether a separator belongs to a directive depends on the text before it, which a lookbehind of fixed length cannot see. A quote of a quoted HTML attribute value that lies inside a directive is not read as common.md#html-attribute-quotes reads it (`<b %%{x: ="}%%x">` and `<b x="%%{x: "}%%foo"`): the tag and quoted-value rules read a directive whole. A common comment region inside a string, label or block (common.md#comment-lines) is colored as a comment inside that scope: the scope continues after the region, and a TextMate grammar cannot leave out part of an open scope. Follows common.md#notation, common.md#where-a-directive-is, common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary, common.md#comment-lines, common.md#html-attribute-quotes, common.md#entities, common.md#leading-whitespace, detection.md#how-to-read-the-list, packet.md#numbers-and-strings, usecase.md#ordered-default-context-rules, packet.md#composite-common-forms, packet.md#hidden-forms, and common.md#reading-a-source.

frontmatter.comment: Embed the frontmatter body as YAML, using the opening indentation for its closing fence. The line-based rule cannot verify the first source line, a following line terminator, or the first-content-line conditions; the shared limitations apply. Follows common.md#frontmatter.
frontmatter.name: meta.frontmatter.mermaid

directive.comment: Read a directive's name and opaque argument. The word-argument alternative precedes the free-text context. The directive variable assembles the same parts for a single-line match; its atomic group prevents backtracking into a different reading when a following component fails. Follows common.md#where-a-directive-is.

patterns.comment: Read the word argument and optional closer in one match. Follows common.md#where-a-directive-is.
patterns.name: meta.directive.mermaid

patterns.comment: After a directive name or colon at physical line end, read the first argument at the continuing scan position; a word argument retains trailing whitespace and an optional closer across lines, while free text keeps its own closing boundary. Follows common.md#where-a-directive-is.
patterns.name: meta.directive.mermaid

patterns.comment: Read the delayed word argument, then its trailing whitespace and optional closer; leave the following body at the first non-whitespace character. Follows common.md#where-a-directive-is.
Read delayed free text only at the first argument position, retaining later word-looking lines until its closer or separator. Follows common.md#where-a-directive-is.

Read the free-text argument in a context, ending at its closer or before a line or paragraph separator. Trailing whitespace can include that separator before a closer. Follows common.md#where-a-directive-is.
patterns.name: meta.directive.mermaid

patterns.comment: Read a free-text argument without taking whitespace immediately before its closer. Follows common.md#where-a-directive-is.
patterns.name: string.unquoted.directive.mermaid

leading-comment-line.comment: Before the header, read common comments and passed bare percent-pair lines after retained hidden directives have been tried. Directives in the leading gap keep their scopes. Follows common.md#comment-lines, common.md#diagram-detection, and common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary.

comment-line.comment: Read a common comment after line whitespace and directives at a comment start. Directives in that prefix keep their scopes; neither percent sign starts a directive, and directives may separate the marks. Follows common.md#comment-lines and common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary.

native-percent-comment.comment: Read a native percent comment with the form used by packet, info, radar, treemap, railroad, wardley and cynefin. Read directives whole. Stop before a separator-led common comment so the enclosing common-comment rule reads it. Follows packet.md#comments-and-common-trivia, common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary, and common.md#comment-lines.
native-percent-comment.name: comment.line.percentage.mermaid

hidden-directive.comment: Read a native hidden directive with the form used by packet, info, radar, railroad, wardley and cynefin. Read directives whole in the opener, body and closer, judging the closing boundary after them. Stop before a separator-led common comment, retaining the single-line match and native-comment fallback. Follows packet.md#hidden-forms, common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary, and common.md#comment-lines.
hidden-directive.name: comment.block.ignored.mermaid

hidden-yaml.comment: Read native hidden YAML with the form used by packet, info, radar, railroad, wardley and cynefin. This context closes at its first qualifying fence, rather than trying the body-present alternative before the adjacent empty form. Read directives in its fences, opening padding and body whole, and common comments independently. Follows packet.md#hidden-forms, common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary, and common.md#comment-lines.
hidden-yaml.name: comment.block.ignored.mermaid

string-escaped.comment: Read matching quotes and backslash escapes for the shared escaped strings of packet, radar, railroad, wardley and cynefin. Common comments are read independently inside the string; agentflow and eventmodeling keep their own comment-preserving contexts. Follows packet.md#numbers-and-strings and common.md#comment-lines.

patterns.name: string.quoted.double.mermaid
constant.character.escape.mermaid
patterns.comment: Read a backslash and its escaped character through whole directives. A backslash before an HTML tag opener leaves that opener for the HTML rule. Follows packet.md#numbers-and-strings, common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary, and common.md#html-attribute-quotes.
Read a double-quoted string; HTML attribute quotes do not close the surrounding string. Follows packet.md#numbers-and-strings and common.md#html-attribute-quotes.

patterns.name: string.quoted.single.mermaid
constant.character.escape.mermaid
patterns.comment: Read a backslash and its escaped character through whole directives; quotes inside those directives do not close the string. Follows packet.md#numbers-and-strings and common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary.
Read a single-quoted string with backslash escapes. Follows packet.md#numbers-and-strings.

string-plain-double.comment: Read the shared plain double-quoted string, without escapes. Common comments are read independently inside it; agentflow and eventmodeling keep their own comment-preserving contexts. Follows kanban.md#the-shape-context and common.md#comment-lines.
string-plain-double.name: string.quoted.double.mermaid

string-plain-single.comment: Read the shared plain single-quoted string, without escapes, as used by treemap and treeview. Common comments are read independently inside it. Follows treemap.md#names-numbers-and-strings and common.md#comment-lines.
string-plain-single.name: string.quoted.single.mermaid

markdown-string.comment: Read a markdown string through its first backquote-plus-double-quote closer. Only the outer delimiters are recognized for flowchart's nested string contexts; agentflow keeps its own comment-preserving context. Delimiter captures keep directives between their characters scoped. Follows usecase.md#ordered-default-context-rules, common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary, and common.md#comment-lines.
markdown-string.name: string.quoted.other.markdown.mermaid

markdown-string-end-scopes.comment: Scope the shared, flowchart and agentflow markdown closer: read directives independently and give only the delimiter characters the string-end scope. Follows usecase.md#ordered-default-context-rules and common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary.

common-statements.comment: Collect the shared title and accessibility forms used by packet, info, radar, treemap, railroad, wardley, cynefin and treeview. Eventmodeling selects its variants from its own rules. Follows packet.md#composite-common-forms.

common-title.comment: Read a padded title with one ASCII space/tab before its possibly empty value, or the bare keyword without a value scope. Values stop before non-directive percent pairs, physical line ends or separator-led common comments. Directives in the gap keep their scopes. Follows packet.md#composite-common-forms, common.md#comment-lines, and common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary.

patterns.comment: Begin the value after the padded keyword and its one ASCII separator; end before a non-directive percent pair, physical line end or separator-led common comment. Follows packet.md#composite-common-forms, common.md#comment-lines, and common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary.

Read a bare title only before whitespace, a percent pair or the end of text, leaving longer names and following punctuation to diagram rules. Follows packet.md#composite-common-forms and wardley.md#keyword-and-name-boundaries.

common-acc-title.comment: Read accTitle, its ASCII padding and colon, then possibly empty line text. Directives in the gap keep their scopes. Stop before non-directive percent pairs, physical line ends or separator-led common comments. Follows packet.md#composite-common-forms, common.md#comment-lines, and common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary.

common-acc-descr-line.comment: Read accDescr, its ASCII padding and colon, then possibly empty line text. Directives in the gap keep their scopes. Stop before non-directive percent pairs, physical line ends or separator-led common comments. Follows packet.md#composite-common-forms, common.md#comment-lines, and common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary.

common-acc-descr-block.comment: Read accDescr, its whitespace gap and braces around description text. These braces delimit text, not a block of statements, members or attributes. Directives in the gap keep their scopes; common comments are read independently inside the value. Follows packet.md#composite-common-forms, common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary, and common.md#comment-lines.

html-tag.comment: Read a complete same-line tag without a scope of its own, preserving the surrounding text scope. Quoted attribute values do not close the surrounding double-quoted string. Read directives whole; one containing the first greater-than sign ends the tag after that directive. Stop before an ordinary double quote or separator-led common comment for the enclosing context to read. Follows common.md#html-attribute-quotes, common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary, and common.md#comment-lines.

escaped-html-tag.comment: Read a same-line tag inside an escaped string. Outside quoted attribute values, read the enclosing string's escape; leave an attribute opener after a backslash for the HTML rule. Leave escapes crossing the tag end or a common-comment boundary for the enclosing string. Keep components whole during backtracking; inside attribute values the first written double quote ends the value even after a backslash. Follows common.md#html-attribute-quotes, packet.md#numbers-and-strings, common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary, and common.md#comment-lines.

entity.comment: Read one entity on one line without a scope of its own, retaining the surrounding text scope and the scopes of internal directives. Follows common.md#entities.

html-tag-preserved-comments.comment: Read a same-line tag with comment-looking text retained for agentflow and eventmodeling. Read directives whole; one containing the first greater-than sign ends the tag after that directive. Follows common.md#html-attribute-quotes, common.md#reading-a-source, and common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary.

markdown-html-tag.comment: Read a same-line tag in markdown without a scope of its own. Attribute quotes are read as single quotes, so backquotes inside quoted attribute values do not close markdown. Outside those values and directives, stop only before the markdown closer or a separator-led common comment. Read directives whole; one containing the first greater-than sign ends the tag after that directive. Follows common.md#html-attribute-quotes, usecase.md#ordered-default-context-rules, common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary, and common.md#comment-lines.

markdown-html-tag-preserved-comments.comment: Read the markdown HTML variant with comment-looking text retained for agentflow. Attribute quotes are read as single quotes, so backquotes inside quoted attribute values do not close markdown. Read directives whole; one containing the first greater-than sign ends the tag after that directive. Follows common.md#html-attribute-quotes, usecase.md#ordered-default-context-rules, common.md#reading-a-source, and common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary.

leading-hidden-directive.comment: Before a header, read a retained directive formed only after global directives are removed, keeping its inner directives visible. Leave passed nonword percent-brace lines to the leading comment rule. Follows common.md#diagram-detection and common.md#where-a-directive-is.
leading-hidden-directive.name: comment.block.ignored.mermaid
